newsitem.title: POLAND: GE, Nissho, Matav buy stakes in Polish telecoms firm.
newsitem.headline: GE, Nissho, Matav buy stakes in Polish telecoms firm.

text.p: U.S. General Electric Capital, Japan's Nissho Iwai Corp. and Israel's Matav Cable Systems Media will take on Tuesday an 11.6 percent stake in Poland's RP Telecom SA (RPT), RPT's president said.

Andrzej Radzyminski told Reuters the three firms bought their stakes in the privately owned RPT from the firm's other shareholders, notably Israel's Dankner Investments and Schamrock Holdings Inc owned by the Roy Disney family.

He said that after the transaction GE Capital, Nissho Iwai and Matav would have 11.6 percent, Dankner Investment's stake would drop to 11.6 percent from 23.5 percent and Goldman Sachs would retain its current 11.6 percent holding.

Schamrock Holdings and its subsidiaries would sell all their shares amounting to 22.9 percent. RPT's other shareholders include its employees, who have 15 percent, with the rest divided among some 240 Polish and foreign firms. @
Radzyminski said RP Telekom, which had licences for telephone services covering areas inhabited by 25 percent of Poland's 40 million population, currently had 40,000 subscribers.
"We already have part of the financing to boost the number of connections to 600,000 by 1999. By the end of this year we should increase the number of subscribers to 200,000," Radzyminski said.
He said the plan of increasing the number of subscribers to 600,000 over the next three years would entail investment of about $600 million. @

The firm was in the process of acquiring a syndicated loan of $115 million from Chase Mahattan Bank and Poland's Bank Handlowy and another $180 million credit from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
Radzyminski also said that to raise more funds RPT wanted to go public within the next 12 months.
However, he said it was too early to say which bourse it would seek to be listed on or what type of securities the company would issue -- shares, convertible bonds or other.
"Our strategic plan envisages that the firm will become public, but I cannot yet say how or on which bourse," he said.

He added that assuming a telephone saturation of 30 lines per 100 inhabitants and spliting the number of new telephone subscribers half-in-half with the state-owned telecoms monopolist TPSA, RPT's licences would allow it to service 1.2 million phones.
He said the cost of setting up each new line was between $800 and $1,000.
Radzyminski said RP Telekom, which currently had a capital of more than $75 million expected shareholders would increase it to $120 million by the end of the year.
